700260101.text: Hello there, Traveler. We meet again.

700260102.text: Your recent commission completion record has been stellar indeed. Why, I'd even say you're one of our star adventurers.

700260104.text: We of the Inazuma Adventurers' Guild are normally in contact with the other branches throughout Teyvat. As such, there is no need for you to be so humble. Your exploits in Mondstadt and Liyue are known to us.

700260107.text: Actually, we'd like you to consider working on a relatively simple investigation. The area to be investigated is on Tsurumi Island.

700260108.text: The weather on the island can be considered quite unique, and it is shrouded in fog all year around. However, investigations should still be relatively safe to conduct.

700260109.text: The Guild normally sends more experienced adventurers to take up this task, but this time, the adventurer we sent canceled the commission soon after arriving on Tsurumi Island.

700260110.text: He did not elaborate much as to his reasons; he just hurriedly explained that it was beyond his abilities and that he was giving it up.

700260111.text: But after this adventurer forfeited, this commission ended up idling here for quite a while without anyone to take it up. The commissioning party has asked after it several times already...

700260112.text: Well then, I thought, we should probably send an adventurer with exceptional survival skills and experience, and have them complete this commission.

700260113.text: That was when you came to mind. So, what do you say, Traveler?

700260106.text: Haha, you are as direct as they say.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the designated location to investigate

700260201.text: Welcome back, Traveler. What did you find?

700260202.text: So, we met this Ruin Grader that won't stay dead...

700260203.text: A strange Ruin Grader that keeps getting back up no matter how many times it is brought down... The person who commissioned this quest didn't say a thing about this.

700260204.text: No wonder that previous adventurer looked so upset. They must've been stumped by that strange Ruin Grader.

700260205.text: ...We should really be informed of such things ahead of time...

700260206.text: I'm sure that I reminded Mr. Hosseini that he should be honest and clear when stating the details of the commission. How could he do something like this?

700260207.text: Unclear wording, missing content, it seems that more and more people are writing commissions this way. How are we supposed to give adventurers work like this? Seriously...

700260209.text: I'm alright, at least. I just wish that the people posting commissions would communicate their needs to the Guild more clearly.

700260212.text: ...My apologies, I spoke out of turn.

700260213.text: Regardless, I believe that the best and least costly way to solve this is to make contact with the person who submitted this commission directly and explain the situation with the reviving Ruin Grader to him.

700260214.text: We shall see if he can accept the investigation results as they are and, if he believes that we can continue investigating, whether he has any way of solving the problem or not.

700260215.text: All I can do is record matters as best as I can. If this commission is to continue, I will do my best to support you all the same.

700260217.text: In that case, I leave the matter of contacting Mr. Hosseini to you.

700260211.text: Well, so is my serving as the intermediary between the guild and the people who post our commissions.

700260304.text: Ahh, I just received a status report from the Adventurers' Guild, and was just wondering if the one who had taken the commission up was you. So it was!

700260306.text: *sigh* I know what you're going to say. Miss Katheryne was just haranguing me back there. I told her that I now understand the situation... More or less.

700260307.text: Would it be correct to say that you encountered a Ruin Grader with regenerative powers at the investigation area?
